name: Jelly Stars
instructions:
- Choose a central point for the firework explosion.
    - Generate multiple particles radiating outward from this central point at evenly spaced angles.
    - Assign each particle a random speed and a random small delay before becoming visible.
    - For each frame, update each particle’s position by moving it outward along its angle, decreasing its speed gradually to simulate slowing.
    - Apply a slight random jitter to each particle’s position on each frame to mimic sparkling.
    - Vary the brightness and size of each particle slightly over time to enhance the sparkling effect.
    - Draw each particle as a small, bright point or star shape, using a glowing or blurred effect to simulate light.
    - Gradually fade out the particles’ opacity until they disappear.

name: Potion Brewing
idea: Seeing from the top view, drop random potion ingredients that creates ripples in the liquid. The ingredients break apart and disappear after a while. There are also random bubbles that appear like the potion is simmering.
instructions:
- Choose the mouse position to drop a potion ingredient.
- Draw the ingredient shape at this position, starting from above and moving downward until it reaches the liquid surface.
- Upon contact with the surface, trigger a ripple effect by drawing expanding, fading circles centered at the impact point.
- Animate the ingredient breaking apart into several smaller pieces, moving outward and fading as they disperse.
- After a short duration, make the ingredient and its fragments disappear completely.
- At random intervals and positions within the liquid area, draw small circles to represent bubbles, animating them rising slightly and fading out to simulate simmering.

name: Fish Whisperer
idea: a pool of fish that will follow my mouse
instructions:
- Determine the current position of the mouse.
- For each fish, calculate the direction vector from the fish’s current position toward the mouse position.
- Adjust the fish’s velocity slightly toward this direction, simulating a natural following behavior.
- Optionally, add a small random variation to each fish’s movement to mimic organic swimming.
- Update the fish’s position based on its velocity.
- Draw the fish at its updated position, orienting its body to face the direction of movement.

name: Metamorphosis
idea: the beautiful moment when a caterpillar turns into a butterfly
instructions:
- Draw a green caterpillar shape with multiple segments near the bottom of the canvas.
- Gradually animate the caterpillar curling up into a small oval shape, representing a chrysalis.
- Fade out the caterpillar’s features as the chrysalis forms, changing its color to a pale green or brown.
- Hold the chrysalis still for a short moment to suggest transformation.
- Animate cracks or gentle glowing lines on the chrysalis to indicate emerging movement.
- Slowly open the chrysalis, revealing butterfly wings with vibrant patterns and colors folded inside.
- Animate the butterfly wings gently unfolding and expanding outward.
- Add details such as antennae and a slender butterfly body as it emerges.
- Animate the butterfly pausing, then gently flapping its wings.
- Animate the butterfly lifting off and floating upward, leaving the empty chrysalis behind.

name: vine
idea: vines grow out of the point of clicking, ending in flowers that pop, spreading their petals and letting them drift downward
instructions:
- Record the click or touch position as the vine’s starting point.
- Create a vine path beginning at that point, with its growth progress initially at zero.
- Each frame, extend the vine gradually upward or outward using a gently curving direction with slight natural variation.
- Draw the grown portion as a narrow, slightly irregular green stem.
- When the vine reaches its planned length, create a flower at its endpoint and begin its blooming phase.
- Start the flower as a small, closed bud, then quickly expand it outward in a popping motion.
- Draw several colorful petals radiating from the flower center, increasing their size and rotation as the bloom opens.
- After the flower reaches full size, detach the petals and give each one a slightly different downward and sideways drifting motion.
- Apply gentle rotation and decreasing downward speed to each falling petal so they flutter naturally.
- Fade the petals gradually as they move away from the flower.
- Remove the animation once the vine and all petals have finished fading.

name: balls
idea: Make alternating red balls and blue balls with each click. Blue and red balls have different sizes
instructions:
- When a mouse click or touch occurs, record its position.
- Track an alternating state that switches between red and blue after each interaction.
- For the current state, choose red with the larger diameter or blue with the smaller diameter.
- Create one ball centered at the recorded position using the selected color and size.
- Animate the ball by gradually changing its size or opacity until it disappears.
- Switch the alternating state so the next interaction produces the other color.

name: bunnies
idea: make a bunny that explodes into smaller bunnies
instructions:
- When a mouse press or touch begins, record the interaction position and create one large bunny centered there.
- Draw the bunny from simple shapes: two ears, a head, two eyes, a nose, a body, and a small tail.
- Start the explosion with the bunny fully visible and a short animation timer at zero.
- Over time, shrink the original bunny while moving its parts slightly outward from the interaction point.
- Replace the original bunny with several smaller bunny shapes positioned around the center.
- Give each smaller bunny its own outward direction, speed, rotation, and starting size.
- During each animation frame, move every smaller bunny outward, rotate it gradually, and reduce its size.
- Fade the smaller bunnies as they shrink.
- Stop drawing the effect when all smaller bunnies have become nearly invisible or moved beyond the canvas.

name: alphabet
idea: multicolored Alphabets appearing after each press - they will sequence incrementally by press so first press is A, then B, and so on
instructions:
- On each mouse or touch press, determine the next alphabet letter from the press count, starting with A.
- Increment the press count so the following press selects the next letter.
- Choose the press location as the letter’s starting position.
- Assign the letter a bright color, cycling through different hues for successive presses.
- Begin the letter small and slightly transparent.
- Draw the letter using a large, bold text style.
- Animate it by expanding its size, spiralling it slightly upward in a random direction, and increasing its opacity.
- Gradually fade the letter out as the animation progresses.
- Remove the animation instance after it becomes fully transparent.

name: purple somethings
instructions:
- When a mouse click or touch occurs, record its position as the effect’s center.
- Create a small purple star or four-point sparkle at that position.
- Give the sparkle a random initial size, rotation, and slight movement direction.
- Over a short lifetime, smoothly increase its brightness and size.
- Make its opacity pulse up and down to create a twinkling effect.
- Rotate the sparkle slowly while it expands.
- Draw it with a vivid purple fill and a softer, translucent purple glow behind it.
- Gradually fade the glow and sparkle until both become fully transparent.
- Remove the effect after its lifetime ends.

name: rainclouds
instructions:
- Position a fluffy cloud above the mouse or touch location.
- Draw the cloud as several overlapping soft circular shapes, using a light gray or white color.
- When the mouse is pressed or the screen is touched, create a stream of rain beneath the cloud.
- Represent each raindrop as a thin blue line or small elongated shape.
- Give each raindrop a slightly different horizontal position, length, and falling speed.
- Move the raindrops downward on every frame.
- When a raindrop reaches the bottom of the animation area, return it to the top of the rain stream.
- Add a subtle vertical bobbing motion to the cloud to make it feel soft and floating.
- Fade the raindrops slightly as they approach the bottom, then restore their brightness when they restart.
- Stop creating or moving the rain when the mouse or touch interaction ends.
